slides.title: Pudu Robotics Unveils PuduFM 1.0 and PuduAgent
slides.tldr: NEW HUMANOID AND EMBODIED AI SYSTEMS
slides.highlight: The introduction of PuduFM 1.0 and PuduAgent advances humanoid and embodied AI systems, providing relevant insights for RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Is Telehealth Better Used to Treat Patients or Help Other Physicians Treat Patients? An Agent-Based Modeling Study of Healthcare Provision
slides.highlight: This study uses agent-based modeling to analyze how physician-to-physician versus physician-to-patient telehealth affects clinical outcomes and system utilization, providing insights for societal-scale simulation of healthcare provision relevant to MIMIC.

card.one_liner: Telehealth is more cost-effective when used for physician-to-physician consultation than for direct patient access.
card.key_idea: An agent-based model simulating medical toxicology care to compare the health outcomes and costs of toxicologist-physician versus toxicologist-patient telehealth and Poison Control Center access.
card.evaluation: Simulated 1,000 patients across 100 runs per scenario. Results were validated against empirical cost-savings data from existing toxicology and PCC literature.
card.limitation: Uses simulated data; assumes perfect in-hospital diagnostic accuracy and that patients have only one medical problem.

slides.title: Modelling Opinion Dynamics at Scale with Deep MARL
slides.tldr: SCALING OPINION DYNAMICS WITH DEEP MARL
slides.highlight: This work uses multi-agent reinforcement learning to model opinion dynamics and conformity in large social networks, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation of human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Deep MARL models opinion dynamics to show how high conformity in large networks promotes misinformation.
card.key_idea: A GPU-accelerated general-sum MARL game using other-play and a learned attention layer to model consensus and truth-finding across large populations.
card.evaluation: Validated on a Bluesky network subset by recovering agent importance from graph topology; compared large social networks against small hunter-gatherer networks.

slides.title: Hierarchical Policies from Verbal and Egocentric Human Signals for Natural Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: The EDITH framework integrates language, first-person view, and gaze to reduce user effort in human-robot interaction. This supports RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: EDITH enables natural human-robot interaction by combining verbal instructions with egocentric view and gaze signals.
card.key_idea: A hierarchical policy using a VLM high-level controller to infer intent and produce subtasks (fine-grained instructions + keyframes) for a VLA low-level executor.
card.evaluation: Tested on three HRI tasks (muffin-serving, tumbler-sorting, tool-passing); achieved 59.7% average success rate, significantly outperforming language-only baselines (<6.5%).
card.limitation: Reactivity is limited by VLM latency and performance degrades for users with physical attributes (e.g., height) differing from training data.

slides.title: UBTECH launches UWORLD U1 humanoid robot companions
slides.highlight: The launch of UWORLD U1 humanoid robot companions is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Personalized and Robust Proactive Robot Assistance with Uncertainty-Guided LLM Reasoning
slides.tldr: PROACTIVE ROBOT ASSISTANCE VIA UNCERTAINTY-GUIDED LLM REASONING
slides.highlight: The GLOBE framework improves proactive robot assistance in noisy household environments by combining Markov models with LLM reasoning. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied AI.

card.one_liner: GLOBE enables proactive robot assistance by combining lightweight Markov models with selective LLM reasoning for object prediction.
card.key_idea: Uses n-gram Markov models for efficient sequential activity and object prediction, invoking an LLM for semantic reasoning only when model confidence falls below a threshold.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on HOMER+ and a new noisy dataset, HOMER-Noise. Compared against SLaTe-PRO and STOT using mean F1-scores; results show competitive accuracy and superior robustness.
card.limitation: Selective LLM invocation introduces significantly higher inference latency compared to purely sequential models due to external API calls.

slides.title: Personality Anchoring for Social Simulation: Linking Personality, Social Behavior, and Interaction Success with LLM Agents
slides.tldr: PERSONALITY ANCHORING FOR LLM SOCIAL SIMULATION
slides.highlight: This research introduces a personality anchoring pipeline for multi-LLM social simulations, demonstrating how personality traits like Agreeableness influence goal achievement and cooperative strategies. It is relevant to MIMIC's focus on LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: Personality anchoring using known characters reveals that dyadic Agreeableness strongly predicts shared goal achievement in LLM simulations.
card.key_idea: The 'personality anchoring' method leverages LLMs' internal knowledge of famous characters to simulate stable personality traits, analyzing how Agreeableness pairings influence conversational strategies and goal success.
card.evaluation: 1,010 conversations across 7 goal categories using LLM-as-a-judge. Results showed high reliability (ICC=0.89) and a monotonic relationship between Agreeableness and success.
card.limitation: Relies on LLM-as-a-judge scoring and pre-existing character knowledge, which may introduce stereotypes and Western cultural biases.

slides.title: Safe, Fluent and Acceptable Motion Generation and Execution for Human--Robot Interaction in Manufacturing Environments
slides.tldr: SOCIAL-AWARE MOTION CONTROL FOR HUMAN-ROBOT INTERACTION
slides.highlight: This research explores integrating social-aware motion control and psycho-cognitive perspectives into robot behavior to improve social acceptability and human comfort, supporting RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A motion control framework for cobots that balances physical safety with human-perceived social acceptability.
card.key_idea: An MPC framework using separating-plane optimization and LSTM-based human motion prediction, parameterized by maximum velocity and interaction distance to generate four distinct socially-informed behaviors.
card.evaluation: Validated via a user study with 111 non-experts using NASA-TLX for workload and 10 bipolar adjective scales for social perception.

slides.title: Titans-as-a-Layer: Test-Time Memory for Conversational Speech Emotion Recognition
slides.highlight: This work introduces a Memory-as-a-Layer adapter to capture dialogue history and emotional context, supporting HyECHO's goal of multimodal social perception of team states.

card.one_liner: MAL adds test-time neural memory to frozen audio LLMs to improve conversational speech emotion recognition.
card.key_idea: A plug-and-play Titans-style memory branch provides audio-token-aligned residual updates, using a two-stage training schedule: first LoRA for task adaptation, then MAL for dialogue-state memory.
card.evaluation: Tested on IEMOCAP, MELD, and MultiDialog using Qwen2-Audio, Audio Flamingo 3, and Ultravox-v0.4. Results show consistent improvements in WA, UA, and WF1.
card.limitation: Broader coverage across more backbone-dataset combinations and comparisons against other memory architectures are still needed.

slides.title: Impedance MPC for Physical Human-Robot Interaction: Predictive Disturbance Rejection with Joint-Limit Safety
slides.tldr: PREDICTIVE IMPEDANCE CONTROL FOR SAFE PHRI
slides.highlight: This work introduces a two-layer Impedance MPC that ensures trajectory accuracy and joint-limit safety during physical human-robot interaction. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A two-layer Impedance MPC achieving zero steady-state error and joint-limit safety for human-robot interaction.
card.key_idea: Analytical feedforward cancellation reduces the plant to a constant-matrix double integrator, enabling a fast convex QP with Kalman-augmented disturbance estimation.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on a 7-DOF Franka FR3 in MuJoCo; outperformed classical impedance with <0.05mm steady-state error under 15N force.
card.limitation: The zero-steady-state-error guarantee applies only to constant or asymptotically constant disturbances, not arbitrary non-convergent drifts.

slides.title: Towards Robust Arabic Speech Emotion Recognition with Deep Learning
slides.highlight: This research evaluates hybrid architectures for Arabic speech emotion recognition, demonstrating that CNN-Transformer models effectively capture spectral and temporal dependencies. This is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement modeling.

card.one_liner: A CNN-Transformer hybrid architecture achieves state-of-the-art accuracy for Arabic speech emotion recognition across two datasets.
card.key_idea: Combines CNNs for local spectral feature extraction with Transformers for global context modeling, outperforming CNN-LSTM and fine-tuned wav2vec 2.0 models.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on EYASE and BAVED datasets using accuracy and F1-score; CNN-Transformer reached 98.1% accuracy on BAVED and 97.1% on EYASE.
card.limitation: Performance is sensitive to noise and exhibits confusion between acoustically similar emotions like happiness and neutrality.

slides.title: Automated Pronunciation Evaluation for Korean Toddler Speech using Speech Diarization and Self-Supervised Learning
slides.highlight: This work utilizes neural speaker diarization and self-supervised learning to evaluate toddler speech, contributing to HyECHO's focus on identity recognition and diarization in challenging acoustic environments.

card.one_liner: An automated pipeline for evaluating Korean toddler pronunciation using speaker diarization and self-supervised learning.
card.key_idea: Combines NeMo SortFormer for diarization with a cross-model ensemble (HuBERT-large for consonants, WavLM-large for vowels) and logistic regression for binary correctness classification.
card.evaluation: Tested on a novel corpus of 53 Korean toddlers (aged 2-5). Achieved 0.782 mean balanced accuracy and 33.04% diarization error rate.
card.limitation: Residual diarization errors from overlapping high-pitched 'aegyo' speech introduce noise into downstream pronunciation classification.

slides.title: Ouvia: A User-centered Framework for Measuring Usability of Speech Translation in Real-World Communication Scenarios
slides.highlight: This work introduces Ouvia to measure the real-world usability of speech translation in one-to-one communication, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: Ouvia is a user-centered framework measuring the real-world usability of speech translation across diverse demographics.
card.key_idea: A multi-phase protocol involving senders, receivers, and bilingual validators to assess if translations successfully convey key information in healthcare and everyday scenarios.
card.evaluation: 1,738 interactions across four ST systems with speakers of three English dialects; found QA-based metrics predict usability better than standard automatic metrics.
card.limitation: Limited to one language pair (English-Portuguese) using clean, scripted speech recorded in noise-free environments, potentially overestimating real-world usability.

slides.title: Decoupling Thought from Speech: Knowledge-Grounded Counterfactual Reasoning for Resilient Multi-Agent Argumentation
slides.tldr: ENHANCING MULTI-AGENT ARGUMENTATION RESILIENCE VIA ARCHITECTURAL DECOUPLING
slides.highlight: This research introduces Knowledge-Grounded Counterfactual Reasoning to prevent logic degradation and role drift in multi-agent debates, supporting MIMIC's focus on stable LLM-based agent models in societal-scale simulations.

card.one_liner: KG-CFR enhances multi-agent debate resilience by decoupling private planning from public execution via knowledge-grounding.
card.key_idea: A dual-stage architecture using a private retrieval-augmented planning buffer for counterfactual reasoning, injecting the resulting strategy into the public executor's context window using recency bias.
card.evaluation: Tested on 270 trajectories in the DRAU environment using Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite; evaluated via LLM judges, expert review, and custom stability metrics.
card.limitation: Increased inference latency, high token overhead, limited to tripartite topologies, and ineffective against affective (ad-hominem) perturbations.
